rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes depositing an AlCrTiZrMo HEA film via Co-FCVAD and annealing, whereas the paper uses mechanically alloyed CrFeNiMo, Co0.5CrFeNiMo, and Al0.5CrFeNiMo powders consolidated by SPS into electrodes and then electrospark-deposited. These are entirely different kinds of intervention (coating deposition method and material system).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high-temperature oxidation at ~800 °C and tribocorrosion, while the paper's conditions involve SPS consolidation (850–1050 °C, 50 MPa, Ar) and ESD under Ar at room temperature with no aggressive-environment or high-temperature performance testing. The conditions are contradictory.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes formation of a dense composite oxide (ZrTiO4) as a protective barrier during annealing. The paper's mechanism involves SPS-temperature-driven diffusion, densification, and pore closure to improve electrode integrity, and ESD-based melt transfer with layer-dependent defect formation. These are different classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved oxidation resistance, hardness, and wear under high-temperature aggressive conditions. The paper measures densification, porosity, bulk hardness of SPS compacts, and coating continuity/defects, with no corrosion or wear testing. The predicted property and direction are not aligned with the paper's measured outcomes.
